test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A 250 m long train running at a speed of 100 km/h crosses another train, coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 62 km/h, in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in opposite direction = 100 + 62 = 162 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s: 162 × (5/18) = 45 m/s.

**Total Distance** covered (Sum of lengths) = Relative Speed × Time = 45 × 10 = 450 m.

**Length of second train** = Total Distance − Length of first train = 450 − 250 = 200 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 250 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 100 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 62 km/h

Time taken (T) = 10 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a86dadc20fd871ebabb57d0fa8164baef9644237e9ab17a7c8e28829f5e99068.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 100 + 62 = 162 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 162 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 9 × 5 = 45 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

⇒ 250 + L₂ = 45 × 10

⇒ 250 + L₂ = 450

⇒ L₂ = 450 − 250

⇒ L₂ = 200 m

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the **same direction**, it is the **difference** (S₁ − S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a **stationary point** (pole, man), distance = Length of train. When it crosses a **platform or another train**, distance = Sum of both lengths.</p
